title: Philly's New Math: LeBron as 'Offense Creator,' Embiid Still Chasing One Thing
author: Rico
summary: The Sixers are reportedly shaping LeBron James into an 'offense creator' this season, while Joel Embiid says the only thing that matters now is winning. Rico on why one of those plans is realistic — and one isn't.

content.value:
## A Role, Not a Throne

ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported this week that the 76ers are planning to use LeBron James as an **"offense creator"** this season — not a go-to scorer, not a third option, but the guy who gets everyone else into their spots. It's a sensible job for a 40-year-old with a pass-first instinct and a defense that still has to respect his shot.

It's also, by the numbers, the role Philadelphia actually needs filled. The Sixers have spent two years trying to figure out who runs the offense when Joel Embiid isn't the one creating it. LeBron solves that on paper.

### Embiid's One Demand

In a separate clip, Embiid was blunt about what this season is for: **"I need to win."** Not stay healthy. Not make an All-Star team. Win.

That's the tension sitting underneath Philadelphia's whole offseason. A LeBron who facilitates is a real plan. A LeBron who still has heavy two-way playoff minutes left in his legs is not a plan — it's a hope.

content.title: RICO'S TAKE
content.sub: LeBron turns 42 in December — "offense creator" still means 30+ minutes a night come the postseason.

content.value: Philadelphia's roster construction is smarter than it's been in years. Whether it's enough for Embiid's one demand depends on a 40-year-old staying exactly that — a creator, not a closer, every single night from October through June.
